messages:
sara.customer: Hey team — after upgrading to @redwood/sdk v2.3.0 our Next.js Edge build passes but runtime fails in prod with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for the SDK import, TS complains about missing types, and API calls return 401s only in the Edge deployment. Local dev works. Anyone seen a combo of exports/types + edge auth issues?

alex.support: Sorry for the trouble. Quick questions: can you paste your package.json exports block and the exact TS/import error? Also which Next version and any custom bundler config (swc/esbuild)?

sara.customer: Sure — relevant parts:
```json
"dependencies": {"@redwood/sdk": "2.3.0"},
"exports": {".": {"import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"}, "./package.json": "./package.json"},
"types": "dist/index.d.ts"
```
TS error from CI build: `TS6053: File 'node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/esm/index.d.ts' not found.`
Runtime log from Edge: `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@redwood/sdk' imported from /var/task/.next/server/pages/index.js`
Also requests from Edge -> /v1/generate return 401 with server response body "missing auth" but same key works from serverless lambda env.

jon-sdk: This looks like a conditional-exports + types resolution edge case. Next's Edge/runtime resolver will prefer the `import` entry (ESM). If the package's `types` def points at a single top-level file that only exists in the CJS build path, TS will try to resolve a `.d.ts` under the ESM path and fail. Separately, some edge runtimes replace global fetch with a polyfill that drops certain headers on redirect or when used through cross-origin fetch wrappers, which can surface as 401s.

mina.engineering: Quick suggestions while we dig in: 1) Confirm Next is building for the `edge` runtime (next.config.js or page runtime). 2) For the auth 401, check if you have a fetch wrapper that calls `new Headers()` then spreads an object — some runtimes don't preserve symbol-backed header entries and auth header can be stripped. 3) For TS/errors: try adding an explicit `exports` subpath for types, like "./types": "./dist/index.d.ts" or include a `types` conditional export.

alex.support: Can you paste the minimal repro steps and the exact Next build command you ran? If we can reproduce locally we can validate a patch quickly.

sara.customer: Repro steps:
1) repo with Next 13.4, edge middleware page that imports `import sdk from '@redwood/sdk'`
2) `npm i @redwood/sdk@2.3.0`
3) `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api... npm run build` (next build)
Logs: 
``
node:internal/modules/esm:719
throw new ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND...
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@redwood/sdk' imported from /workspace/.next/server/pages/index.js
TS6053: File 'node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/esm/index.d.ts' not found.

fetch to https://api... returned 401 {"error":"missing auth"}
``

jon-sdk: Temporary workarounds while we ship a fix: 1) pin to 2.2.1 which used a slightly different exports layout, 2) import the CJS entry directly: `import sdk from '@redwood/sdk/dist/cjs/index.cjs'` (not ideal), or 3) add a tiny shim in your project root `node_modules/@redwood/sdk/index.js` with `module.exports = require('./dist/cjs/index.cjs')` and a matching `index.d.ts` that re-exports types.

mina.engineering: We'll prioritize a patch: add a conditional types export and a tiny ESM userland entry so Next edge resolver can find both runtime and d.ts consistently. We'll also audit the fetch usage to reproduce the header drop. I can cut a 2.3.1 patch today if we confirm repro.

alex.support: Can you open a support ticket and attach the minimal repro repo and CI build logs? If you include repo permissions I can escalate to SDK team immediately.

sara.customer: Done — ticket SUP-3421 created and I've added a minimal repro repo and CI logs. Thanks! :pray:

deploy-bot: NOTE: sdk-team scheduled a hotfix branch for 2.3.1 to address conditional `types` export + ESM entry. ETA 8h (will post changelog when released).

jon-sdk: Follow-ups for the ticket: please include package-lock/yarn.lock (lockfile) and your bundler config. There are known failure modes when consumers have multiple versions of rollup/esbuild plugins in the tree (peerDeps conflict).

alex.support: We'll update SUP-3421 with recommended short-term mitigations and the patch ETA. If the workaround isn't feasible, let us know and we'll assist with a small shim patch in your repo until 2.3.1 is released.
